subject: Variable-length data items
notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. WiseOwl COBOL's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 3 (main program GOBACK/STOP): the run unit ends and every managed object of the run unit is reclaimed (process exit or RunUnit teardown). Nothing to observe; no dedicated mechanism is needed or permitted to be observable.
